other_failure_modes.name: Test Set Data Leakage via Imputation
other_failure_modes.description: The agent imputes missing values in the test set using the test set's own median, rather than the training set's median. This uses future/test information to process the test set, which would be unavailable in a real-world production scenario.

other_failure_modes.name: Cross-Validation Leakage
other_failure_modes.description: The agent scales the data and imputes missing values on the entire training dataset before performing cross-validation splits. This leaks information (mean/std and median) from the validation folds into the training folds, making the CV scores overly optimistic.

other_failure_modes.name: Unhandled Categorical Features
other_failure_modes.description: The agent blindly applies median imputation and standard scaling to all feature columns. If the dataset contains any categorical string columns (which is common in financial records), these operations will result in an execution crash.

summary: The agent sets up a basic LightGBM model with 5-fold cross-validation but fails to perform any feature engineering. Critical issues include test set data leakage by imputing missing test data with test-set medians, and cross-validation leakage by applying imputation and scaling before the CV split. Furthermore, the naive application of numeric operations to all columns will likely cause the script to crash on categorical features.
